definition: The fraction of actual negatives correctly identified — specificity, the mirror of recall for the negative class.
details: The fraction of actual negatives correctly identified — specificity, the mirror of recall for the negative class.

explainer.lead: The true negative rate is the fraction of actual negatives that a model correctly identifies, also called specificity. It matters because it is the mirror of recall for the negative class.

tiers.eli5: Of all the things that really are 'no', how many did the model correctly call 'no'.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use this rate to check how well a model avoids flagging negatives as positives; a common pitfall is reading it in isolation while ignoring the false positive count that the rate hides.
tiers.paperLevel: True negative rate is the fraction of actual negatives correctly identified, i.e. specificity, the mirror of recall for the negative class.

explainer.example: If 90 of 100 actual negatives are correctly classified as negative, the true negative rate is 0.9.
